That already sounded ambitious. Now, a fresh leak adds two more names to the Galaxy Z guest list, and one suggests Samsung’s next trick might involve less folding and more stretching. title: Bye bye One UI, hello Galaxy OS? Wild rumor points to a big shakeup for Samsung phones
summary: Samsung might be cooking up a new identity for its Galaxy software.
body: TL;DR A new rumor suggests Samsung could be working on Galaxy OS, with deeper AI integration through Google and third-party partnerships. The tipster claims One UI 10 could bring a major overhaul alongside the Galaxy S28 series. Samsung hasn’t confirmed any of these plans, and no other reliable sources have corroborated the rumor. Samsung has called its Android software One UI for years, and Galaxy users have seen it change quite a bit along the way. We’ve had visual overhauls, new customization options, and, more recently, a growing list of Galaxy AI features . But Samsung may be planning something even bigger for its next major software update, and it could come with a new name. According to an X user known as Phonefuturist , Samsung could be working on something called Galaxy OS . The tipster claims that Samsung is strengthening its partnership with Google and exploring deeper AI integration across its software. It could also partner with third-party services, some of which may be paid, though the details are still unclear.

title: Inside Starlight Festival’s Historic Debut at the Great Pyramids of Giza
summary: Charlotte de Witte, Michael Bibi, Adriatique and more performed at the sold-out festival, which welcomed fans from 114 countries and marked a new chapter for Egypt’s electronic music scene.
body: The Great Pyramids of Giza became the backdrop for one of electronic music’s most ambitious destination festivals as EXIT and P+US, Venture Lifestyle’s electronic music platform, brought the inaugural Starlight Festival to Egypt on Oct. 9 and 10. The sold-out event marked the first multi-day, multi-stage electronic music festival staged at Giza, bringing together more than 60 international and regional artists and attendees from 114 countries. Organizers said it was also the largest electronic music event held at the historic site, since a concert by French pioneer Jean-Michel Jarre held in 1999. Belgian techno heavyweight Charlotte de Witte made her Egyptian debut alongside a lineup featuring Michael Bibi, Adriatique, Indira Paganotto, Enrico Sangiuliano, Vintage Culture, Pete Tong and WhoMadeWho. Beyond the main stage, EXIT’s No Sleep stage hosted Charlie Sparks, BIIA, Layla Benitez, Paolo Ferrara and Olympe, while live performances from Satori and Giolì & Assia added another dimension to the weekend. title: You can now (unofficially) play Super Mario Galaxy on Android, no emulator needed
summary: You don't need a flagship phone to play this, either.
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR A developer has just released an unofficial port of Super Mario Galaxy on Android. There are some notable glitches at this juncture, but performance is otherwise great on even budget Android devices. The port comes roughly two weeks after the Wii game was first decompiled. We saw a major milestone recently as Super Mario Galaxy became the first Wii game to be fully decompiled . This reverse-engineering milestone opens the door to fan ports of the game on other platforms, while also helping the community understand its inner workings. Now, developer Mohammed Huzaifa has released an unofficial Super Mario Galaxy port on Android, called Galaxy-Android. This port, which is available on GitHub , is indeed based on the aforementioned decompilation, though the developer also clarifies that it was an “AI-assisted” port.

title: We asked how you feel about yearly smartphone launches, and the results are depressing
summary: Even Android enthusiasts are getting bored of annual smartphone launches.
body: We’re an enthusiast-first website, and that’s precisely why results from a recent poll we ran are particularly telling. There was a time when a new smartphone launch was genuinely something to look forward to. With an audience like ours — people who follow the smartphone industry closely — you’d expect excitement surrounding annual smartphone launches to be high. That doesn’t seem to be the case. We asked our readers how they feel about annual smartphone launches, and only 5% of respondents showed any meaningful excitement. The majority, on the other hand, said that they were starting to lose interest.

title: 5 One UI settings I always turn off on my Samsung Galaxy phone

body: My primary smartphone is an Android, and unless I’m testing a new device, I almost always use a Galaxy phone. I find One UI the best Android interface out there currently. That said, I can’t use One UI in its default settings: some aren’t configured to my preferences, while others are overly privacy-invasive and harvest data in the background. title: Motorola Signature 27’s seven-year update promise comes with a pretty big asterisk
summary: The Signature 27 sounds like Motorola's software comeback until you read the fine print.
body: TL;DR The Motorola Signature 27 is scheduled to receive up to seven major Android OS updates and bi-monthly security updates for up to seven years. Unlike recent Pixel and Galaxy flagships, Motorola isn’t promising monthly security patches, and even its two-month cadence isn’t guaranteed. Some Motorola fans are fine with fewer, more stable updates, while others are more concerned about those two words: “up to.” Motorola’s software reputation has never quite matched the appeal of its hardware. Its phones can be fast, stylish, and packed with clever ideas, but software update support often becomes the part buyers grumble about later . The Signature 27 looked like a chance to rewrite that story, with Motorola finally putting together a proper premium flagship aimed at the same buyers considering a Pixel or Galaxy. Now we know what that phone’s software support actually looks like, and the headline sounds better than the fine print. Motorola says the Signature 27 is scheduled to receive up to seven major Android OS updates, along with bi-monthly security updates for up to seven years. That sounds generous until you start pulling at the wording.

title: Galaxy Watch 8, Watch Ultra get another One UI 9 beta to chew on while waiting for a stable release
summary: Galaxy Watch 7 gets a slice of the pie too.
body: Credit: Kaitlyn Cimino / Android Authority TL;DR Samsung is rolling out newer One UI 9 Watch beta builds for Galaxy Watch 8, Watch 7, and Watch Ultra. The update brings October’s security patch along with some bug fixes. There’s no information about a stable release yet. After releasing stable One UI 9 for the Galaxy S26 series around the end of September, Samsung is now rapidly progressing and making it available to the oldest eligible flagship models . Over the last couple of weeks, the Galaxy S25, S24, S23, and older foldables have received the stable update. So Samsung’s next priority, naturally, is to bring older Galaxy Watch models up to speed with the latest smartwatches it released this July . For this, Samsung has been running betas for One UI 9 Watch across various Galaxy Watch models. While the stable release is still far off, Samsung is pushing out newer betas to existing testers.

title: Survey shows that most of us aren’t adventurous when it comes to weather apps

body: Sometimes the reason for choosing a weather app can be as fickle as the weather itself: it’s the nicest-looking one in the Play Store, the widget for it lets you make decisions about your outerwear at a glance, or it’s the default one that came with your phone and you don’t want to spend time evaluating any others. title: Qualcomm’s lengthy legal battle with Arm nets it $2 (not a typo) in damages
summary: Two dollars today, potentially billions tomorrow.
body: TL;DR A Delaware jury has awarded Qualcomm $2 in damages in its legal fight with Arm. The jury sided with Qualcomm on two counts, and with Arm on five counts. The legal battle will now go to a US federal judge who will resolve several other issues. Qualcomm and Arm have been involved in a series of legal battles over several issues over the last couple of years. Since Qualcomm acquired Nuvia back in 2021, Arm has threatened to cancel Qualcomm’s architecture licensing agreement (ALA), and Qualcomm has filed lawsuits against Arm. According to a Reuters report, the verdict is finally in for Qualcomm’s latest lawsuit against Arm. The Delaware jury has sided with Qualcomm on two counts, awarding it damages amounting to $2. Yes, that’s not a typo.

title: ANBERNIC’s new Nintendo 3DS lookalike might cost more than expected

body: Credit: YouTube TL;DR Leaked AliExpress listings suggest the ANBERNIC RG DDS could cost $300 to $365, well above expectations for a sub-$250 Nintendo 3DS lookalike. Pre-sales could begin October 16 with a $15 discount, with shipping starting December 10, 2026. ANBERNIC has also shared official footage showcasing 3DS titles running at up to 5x resolution, as well as Wii U, PS3, Xbox, and Android games. After showing it off last week, ANBERNIC is gearing up for a full launch of the RG DDS , its ambitious dual-screen clamshell emulator built for high-end Nintendo 3DS gaming. However, interested buyers might need deeper pockets than initially anticipated, as pricing details have surfaced earlier than expected. Reddit user landblord unearthed an unlisted page on ANBERNIC’s AliExpress store profile. The listing indicates that the RG DDS could be priced between $300 and $365, depending on regional conversions and configurations. That sits well above the community’s hopes for an aggressive sub-$250 price tag, putting the clamshell within striking distance of powerhouse alternatives like the AYN Thor Base .

title: Lemon is a new Switch emulator for Android that picks up where Yuzu left off
summary: The Lemon emulator for Android even offers a Lite version for those with weaker devices.
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR A new Nintendo Switch emulator called Lemon has recently been released on Android. The app is based on Yuzu and was originally made for Snapdragon-powered devices, but has since received Mali GPU support. Lemon offers features like easy data transfer from rival Switch emulators, frame generation, and per-game controller layouts. We’ve seen plenty of Nintendo Switch emulators on Android over the past few years, although Nintendo has cracked down on some of them via legal threats. Now, a new Switch emulator has arrived on Android. Lemon is a Nintendo Switch emulator for Android that’s based on the Yuzu emulator project. The app was first released last month and has been receiving a steady stream of updates since then.

body: Credit: Rushil Agrawal / Android Authority TL;DR A trusted source has revealed that the Samsung Galaxy A58 will retain the same cameras as the Galaxy A57. Update: October 15, 2026 (7:20 AM ET): There’s also bad news if you were hoping that the Galaxy A38 5G would receive camera hardware upgrades. Rounding out the package is a 12MP selfie camera. It’s possible that the Galaxy A38 5G could get other upgrades like a larger battery, improved screen, or faster processor. title: Google will pay you up to $20,000 for Chrome security bugs
summary: It's also adding new categories to the reward program.
body: TL;DR Google is quadrupling the base reward amount for reporting critical Chrome vulnerabilities. It is also introducing rewards of up to $20,000 for high-impact bugs. End-of-year awards will celebrate submissions from the community. Google has relied on vulnerability reports from security researchers alongside its own internal security teams to keep apps like Chrome secure against exploits. The company has made several changes to its Vulnerability Rewards Program (VRP) over the last few months, including reducing Chrome reward payouts in May and using AI to improve Chrome security in July. Now, the company is making further adjustments to the Chrome VRP. In a blog post, the company announces new reward amounts and categories. Google has quadrupled the base reward amount for memory corruption vulnerabilities to $2,000. Furthermore, reports for controlled reads and crashes in the browser, GPU, and network processes will now earn rewards of $4,000. Payouts for controlled writes, on the other hand, can go up to $20,000.
